codeReview.summary: Reviewed commit 452bb463 (worker d378464d, backend-worker skill, followedProcedure true, no deviations) against VAL-FND-015..024, reading the current on-disk code, the contract, architecture.md and library/staffing-patterns.md; no product code or databases were modified. What holds up: token minting (apps/app/app/utils/reservations/token.ts + token.server.ts) matches VAL-FND-016 exactly (HS256 typ 'rsv+jwt', aud 'tenant-api-reservations-operator', role 'operator', region-derived tenantApiUrl 3007/3009, locationScope intersection with null-when-all, 900 s/300 s TTL, 404 master-off, 404 payments-off, 403 grantless, 'Cache-Control: private, no-store', and the exact response shape); reservations-auth.ts/rsvGuard enforce signature, aud, typ, exp-iat cap, region, scope, grants with implied reads, impersonated-write 403, child-flag 404 through the features claim, and allowsLocation with [] allowing nothing; org-router.ts adds the operator-JWT branch, the Origin-bound /reservations/* branch that never trusts query/body orgId, and body-orgId branches for /internal/reservations/*, /api/reservations/* and /api/voice/actions/*; withReservationWrite does runExclusive(orgId) + retryOnSqliteBusy + one transaction (expiry sweep, (scope,key)/request_hash idempotency with 409 idempotency_conflict, fresh day state, version bump, post-commit invalidation/hooks) and its test proves serialization, replay, 409 and the in-tx sweep; the App context route authenticates first (302 rewritten to 403), returns no-store and a schema-valid zero-PII payload; role presets/implied permissions and the role-editor flag gating work; the sidebar/nav gating and reservations+/ route 404s when the flag is off are correct; the seed script is upsert-based and idempotent for acme and riyadh-grill and applies migrations via provisionTenantDb. Verdict: fail on five blocking gaps: (1) the reservations-context cache uses 60 s fresh / 5 min stale and has no failure cooldown, while VAL-FND-018 and architecture.md 456-459 require 5 min fresh / 24 h stale / 30 s cooldown (the sibling scope-context.ts the architecture says to copy has exactly those numbers); (2) no path enforces 'organization provisioned' (VAL-FND-017), so an active org with hasProvisionedDb = false is served from a freshly created empty tenant DB instead of a uniform refusal - the staffing mirror (staff-auth.ts:167) does check it; (3) reservations-security.test.ts omits three of the token variants VAL-FND-020 requires across every mounted route (a 'tenant-api-operator' audience token, an over-long TTL token, an impersonated write) even though library/staffing-patterns.md:94 names the tenant-api-operator case; (4) _layout.tsx never hides the location picker for a single-location organization (VAL-FND-022), so riyadh-grill renders a one-option selector; (5) docs/permissions.md, docs/reservations-contract.md and ADR 048 document a token/permission vocabulary that does not exist in the code (aud 'tenant-api-reservations', claims org/reg/scp/imp, grants read:reservations:any / read:guestbook:any / refund:reservations_payments:any, header X-Internal-Token, migration 0023), so the 8 implemented permissions and the 6 flags are not the ones listed (VAL-FND-024). Non-blocking: role-presets.ts defines 7 presets where the contract says 4 (the four named ones carry the exact required grants; Shift manager/Guestbook manager/Finance are additive), mapSqliteConstraintError matches 'overlap_conflict' while the trigger raises 'table_overlap' (latent 500 instead of 409), the ADR draft omits several listed topics, the idempotency-replay path skips the day-version bump for dates expired by the in-tx sweep, the settings scaffold writes outside withReservationWrite, the public scaffolds proceed when flags are unknown, and notifyReservationsContextChanged has no caller.

issues.description: Cache lifetimes contradict the approved contract. VAL-FND-018 (validation-contract.md:112-117) requires the context cache to be '5 min fresh, 24 h stale, 30 s failure cooldown, 3 s timeout, redirect: error', and architecture.md:456-459 states the same numbers ('Cache in apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-context.ts, copying lib/scope-context.ts: LRU per org, fresh 5 min, stale 24 h, 30 s failure cooldown, 3 s timeout, redirect: error'). The shipped module uses RESERVATIONS_CONTEXT_FRESH_TTL_MS = 60 * 1000 and RESERVATIONS_CONTEXT_STALE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 (lines 10-11), gives the LRU a 5-minute ttl (lines 18-21) and has no failure cooldown at all (getReservationsContext, lines 76-99: every request past the 60 s window re-fetches, even after a failed fetch). Only the 3 s timeout and redirect: 'error' match (lines 46-47). Concrete affected behavior: a control-plane outage now makes every regional request pay the full 3 s timeout (the cooldown exists precisely to prevent that, scope-context.ts:66-75), and stale facts older than 5 minutes are dropped instead of served for up to 24 h, which is the mechanism the architecture relies on for public reads ('Public reads accept stale facts', architecture.md:461-462). The deviation is baked into apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-context.test.ts:107-156, which asserts 60 s/5 min, so the contract's numbers are untested. If the validator decides the contract/architecture numbers are obsolete, the contract and architecture text must be amended together with the test; as written the contract is authoritative.

'Active and provisioned organization' is only half enforced. VAL-FND-017 (validation-contract.md:106-111) requires reservations-auth.ts/reservations-guard.ts to enforce 'active and provisioned organization', and architecture.md:1320-1326 puts 'organization active and provisioned' in the guard's verification path; library/staffing-patterns.md:43 lists the mirror as 'active org 404, provisioned 404'. The shipped code checks neither in reservations-auth.ts (verifyReservationsOperatorToken, lines 54-199, never looks up the organization) nor in reservations-guard.ts (rsvGuard, lines 36-82); each handler calls ensureActiveOrgInNodeRegion (reservations-operator.ts:30-47), which checks existence (findActiveOrganizationById only returns organizations with active = true, apps/app/app/routes/resources+/tenant-organization.ts:30-36) and region, but never hasProvisionedDb. The staffing equivalent does check it: apps/tenant-api/src/lib/staff-auth.ts:159-171 returns 404 'Organization is not provisioned in this region' when !organization.hasProvisionedDb. Failure path: an active organization whose tenant DB was never provisioned (or whose provisioning failed) passes the guard; getTenantDb then creates and migrates a fresh database (packages/tenant-db/src/db.server.ts:106-147, createIfMissing + applyTenantMigrations) and every operator route answers 200 with empty data instead of refusing, which violates the module's fail-closed rule for 'unprovisioned DB' (architecture.md:202-204). No test covers it: the security sweep's fixtures all set hasProvisionedDb: true (reservations-security.test.ts:167-190). Fix: return 404 from the shared org/region check when organization.hasProvisionedDb is false (and add a sweep case).

The security sweep does not cover three token variants the contract requires across every mounted operator route. VAL-FND-020 (validation-contract.md:124-129) says the sweep asserts that 'every operator route returns 401 for missing, bad-secret, wrong-audience (including staffing and tenant-api-operator tokens), wrong-typ, or over-long TTL tokens; 403 for grantless, wrong-scope, or impersonated-write tokens'. The delivered file covers missing (lines 207-218), wrong-secret + wrong-audience + wrong-typ (220-243) and region mismatch (245-258) over the discovered route list, plus grantless in every scope (260-277) and spot checks for cross-org/cross-location (279-364). Missing: (a) the 'tenant-api-operator' audience token - the only wrong audience tested is 'tenant-api-staffing' (line 225), although the generic operator audience really exists (packages/reports/src/operator-token.ts:16, apps/tenant-api/src/routes/operator.ts:66) and library/staffing-patterns.md:94 explicitly requires 'wrong-audience cases (staffing token, tenant-api-operator token)'; (b) over-long TTL - mintRsvToken exposes ttlSeconds (line 118) but no case uses it, so a 901 s token is never asserted to 401 across routes (the only TTL-cap assertion is on one synthetic route, reservations-auth.test.ts:263-274); (c) impersonated-write - mintRsvToken exposes impersonated (line 117) but no case uses it, so write routes are never swept for the 403 impersonated_read_only path (again only one synthetic route, reservations-auth.test.ts:248-261); (d) cross-organization and excluded-locationIds are checked on two routes rather than every route. The runtime checks exist in code, so this is a verification-gate gap, but it is the exact gate the mission treats as mandatory ('every new tenant-api reservations route is added to reservations-security.test.ts', mission AGENTS.md) and it is cheap to close by adding the three token variants to the existing per-route loops.

The single-location location picker is never hidden. VAL-FND-022 (validation-contract.md:137-143) requires the layout to mount ReservationsClientProvider '(hiding the location picker when the organization has only one location)'. The shell always renders the Location select (lines 182-209): it only special-cases locations.length === 0 with a 'Main location' option, and there is no length === 1 branch anywhere in the reservations routes (grep for a single-location condition in apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/reservations+/ returns nothing). The staffing screens use the expected pattern (apps/app/app/routes/_app+/$orgSlug_+/staff+/team.import.tsx:343, 'scopes.length > 1 ? ... : ...'). Observed consequence in the handoff's own browser check: for riyadh-grill, which has exactly one location, the header controls render a one-option Location selector instead of hiding it. Everything else in VAL-FND-022 is implemented (the loader awaits requireReservationsAccess at line 29, ReservationsClientProvider mounts at line 150, and _index.tsx redirects to firstVisibleReservationsPath).

The documentation deliverable lists a permission/flag vocabulary that does not exist in the implementation, so the 8 implemented permissions and the 6 flags are not actually listed (VAL-FND-024, validation-contract.md:151-157). docs/permissions.md:198-205 lists read:reservations:any, update:reservations:any, read:guestbook:any, update:guestbook:any, read:reservations_settings:any, update:reservations_settings:any, read:reservations_reports:any and refund:reservations_payments:any; the shipped permissions are read:reservation:any, update:reservation:any, read:reservation_settings:any, update:reservation_settings:any, read:reservation_guest:any, update:reservation_guest:any, read:reservation_report:any and update:reservation_payment:any (packages/reservations/src/permissions.ts:5-14, packages/auth/src/organization-permissions.server.ts:238-245, packages/database/drizzle/0025_reservations_foundation.sql:5-12). The same file names migration '0023_reservations_foundation' (line 190) where the shipped control-plane migration is 0025 (0023 is staffing_restaurant_locations.sql), documents the implied-read rules and presets with the wrong names (lines 212-224), uses claim 'imp: true' and the guestbook/refund sensitive grants (lines 237-242), and never lists the 6 reservations.* feature flags (only reservations.enabled appears). docs/reservations-contract.md repeats the same vocabulary (line 15 aud 'tenant-api-reservations' instead of 'tenant-api-reservations-operator' from packages/reservations/src/token.ts:12-13; lines 16-30 claims scp/org/reg/imp instead of scope/orgId/region/impersonated; lines 34-40 'X-Internal-Token' where the code sends and checks 'Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN>', apps/app/app/routes/resources+/reservations.context.ts:91 and apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-internal.ts:29; lines 48-56 the non-existent permission names), and ADR 048 does the same (lines 62-64, 85-92, 121-128). Since later milestones implement public routes and voice actions against these names, the docs as written will steer them to non-existent grants and the wrong audience. If the validator decides the architecture's older naming is the intended one, the contract's VAL-FND-015/016/017 strings and the shipped migration/permissions would have to be amended instead; per the review rules the contract governs.

VAL-FND-015 (validation-contract.md:93-99) says the file 'defines the 4 presets' and architecture.md:399 lists 4 (Host, Reservations manager, Guest relations, Owner); RESERVATIONS_ROLE_PRESETS defines 7 keys (RESERVATIONS_ROLE_PRESET_KEYS, lines 12-20) - host, shift_manager, reservations_manager, guest_relations, guestbook_manager, finance, owner - because the feature record asked for Shift manager/Guestbook manager/Finance as well. The four contract presets carry exactly the required grants (Host read/update:reservation; Reservations manager all 7 except update:reservation_payment; Guest relations read:reservation + read/update:reservation_guest; Owner all 8, packages/reservations/src/permissions.ts:136-191), so this is additive scope, not a missing grant set; only a validator that asserts an exact count of 4 would fail. Worth an explicit note in the docs/contract rather than silent divergence.

mapSqliteConstraintError maps the wrong string for table overlap: it checks message.includes('overlap_conflict') (line 575), but the shipped trigger raises 'table_overlap' (packages/tenant-db/drizzle/0016_reservations_foundation.sql:806,819) and no artifact anywhere raises 'overlap_conflict'. Latent today because no mounted foundation route writes occupancies, but the first milestone that seats a table through withReservationWrite will surface a raw error as HTTP 500 from the Hono onError handler instead of a mapped 409 conflict. The sibling review of the migrations feature already recorded the same interface mismatch from the trigger side (fnd-migrations-tenant-and-control-plane.json, non-blocking issue on line 831 and the sharedState note), so this fix and that string decision should land together.

The ADR draft omits several topics VAL-FND-024 (validation-contract.md:151-157) and architecture.md:2521 list for it. Present: placement (section 1), browser-direct operator tokens (2), Origin-bound public routes (3), non-PII context pull (4), write gate (5), erasure and region switching (6), flags and location scope. Missing: guest identity without login (no section; the only guest-identity text is about erasure), payments split (section 12 / US Stripe vs KSA Checkout.com is not described; only 'payment provider credentials' is mentioned at lines 67-69), the shared org alarm / tick generalization, and messaging regions (no SMS/email region discussion). It is a draft that architecture.md says is finalized in native-apps, and the contract's evidence bar is file existence plus headings, so this is non-blocking, but the topics should be added now while the feature is in context.

On an idempotency replay the transaction returns right after the expiry sweep (lines 646-679) and never reaches the post-mutation day-version bump loop (lines 751-761). The swept rows can free capacity on dates recorded by markAffectedDate (lines 651-653), so a replayed request that expires holds/payments/requests/waitlist offers commits those expirations without incrementing rsv_day_versions for the affected (locationId, businessDate) pairs; polling clients keyed on dayVersion will not notice the capacity change until some other write bumps the date. The day cache is still invalidated (lines 799-803) and the replay path is intentionally side-effect free otherwise, so this is a narrow consistency gap rather than a correctness break.

POST /setup/locations/:locationId/settings writes rsv_location_settings directly with db.insert(...).onConflictDoUpdate (lines 149-186) instead of going through withReservationWrite, and it does not bump rsv_day_versions, while mission AGENTS.md states 'every reservation write goes through withReservationWrite' and architecture.md:427-429 expects a settings edit that changes availability to bump the same day versions. This is a foundation scaffold whose full behavior belongs to the setup milestone, and the write is not capacity-consuming, so it is non-blocking; the setup milestone should route it through the gate and bump the affected dates.

The public scaffold fails open when the organization context is unavailable: resolvePublicOrg only refuses when getReservationsContext returns a context whose features are off (lines 68-74), so a null context (App unreachable, misconfigured APP_URL/token, or no cache entry) lets GET /reservations/config serve data and POST /reservations/holds answer ok:true without any flag check. architecture.md:202-204 and 463-465 require fail-closed behavior for public writes ('unreachable App context for public writes: refuse', 'App unreachable -> 503 unavailable'), and the careers pattern it mirrors returns 503 in that case (library/staffing-patterns.md:86). Non-blocking because these are explicitly foundation scaffolds whose real bodies land in online-booking, but the flag check should not stay fail-open.

notifyReservationsContextChanged is exported but has no caller anywhere in apps/app (grep finds only the definition), so no App mutation evicts the regional context cache; ADR 048 lines 129-131 and architecture.md:435-469 assume the App pushes POST /internal/reservations/context-changed when locations, flags, branding or payment accounts change. The endpoint itself works (reservations-internal.ts:68-82, asserted by reservations-security.test.ts:417-502), and the 60 s fresh TTL limits staleness, so this is non-blocking; wiring it into the settings/flag/location actions belongs with the milestones that own those actions.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission has two competing vocabularies for the reservations token and permissions, and only the code has the real one. The feature record, docs/decisions/048, docs/reservations-contract.md and docs/permissions.md use aud 'tenant-api-reservations', claims org/reg/scp/imp, grants read:reservations:any / read:guestbook:any / refund:reservations_payments:any, header X-Internal-Token and migration 0023, while the shipped code uses aud 'tenant-api-reservations-operator', claims orgId/region/scope/impersonated, the 8 read/update:reservation* grants, Authorization: Bearer <INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN> and migration 0025. The canonical strings exist only in code (packages/reservations/src/permissions.ts + token.ts, packages/database/drizzle/0025_reservations_foundation.sql, packages/auth/src/organization-permissions.server.ts). library/staffing-patterns.md:41 has the correct audience but nothing else, so every worker and validator that starts from the docs will use the wrong names. Suggest the mission AGENTS.md or library carry the canonical 8 permission strings, 6 flag keys, token claim names and the internal auth header, and that the validator decide which side (docs vs contract/code) is amended.

The security-sweep requirements that the delivered sweep missed are documented only as a table row in the library, not in the skill or mission AGENTS.md that workers read first. library/staffing-patterns.md:94 requires the reservations sweep to include 'wrong-audience cases (staffing token, tenant-api-operator token), wrong-scope, cross-org (ORG_B), cross-location (locationIds) and capability-token cases', and line 43 lists 'active org 404, provisioned 404' in the staff-auth mirror table that reservations-auth.ts was to copy; the mission AGENTS.md 'Security gates' bullet and the backend-worker skill step 3 only say 'every new route ... wrong-audience' without enumerating the token variants, and the sweep shipped with staffing-only wrong-audience, no over-long TTL and no impersonated-write case, and the guard shipped without the provisioned check. Adding the explicit variant list (and 'provisioned 404') to the skill/AGENTS would have prevented both blocking findings.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: library/staffing-patterns.md:43,94; mission AGENTS.md 'Security gates' directive; skills/backend-worker/SKILL.md step 3 'Security sweep' bullet; apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-security.test.ts:220-243; apps/tenant-api/src/lib/staff-auth.ts:159-171

sharedStateObservations.observation: The architecture's context-cache contract (5 min fresh / 24 h stale / 30 s failure cooldown, 'copying lib/scope-context.ts') lives only in architecture.md:456-459; the library's one-line note for reservations ('a reservations context route and a context cache', library/staffing-patterns.md:102) drops the numbers, and the neighbouring careers cache has different numbers (60 s/15 s, line 86), so the worker re-derived 60 s/5 min. Recording the cache parameters (or 'mirror lib/scope-context.ts exactly') next to the pattern reference would keep the next cache copy aligned with the contract.

summary: Reviewed fnd-auth-routing-guards-and-seed (commit 452bb463, worker d378464d, backend-worker skill, no procedural deviations) against VAL-FND-015..024. Most of the foundation is implemented correctly and is well tested: token minting matches VAL-FND-016 (rsv+jwt, aud tenant-api-reservations-operator, 900/300 s TTL, locationScope intersection, 404/403 refusals, no-store, exact response shape); rsvGuard/reservations-auth enforce signature, aud, typ, TTL cap, region, scope, grants, impersonation and child flags; org-router adds all required branches without trusting client orgId; withReservationWrite implements the serialized sweep/idempotency/version-bump gate with real-SQLite tests; the App context route authenticates first, rewrites 302 to 403 and returns a schema-valid zero-PII payload; role presets/implied permissions and role-editor flag gating work; sidebar/route 404 gating and the _index redirect work; the seed script is idempotent for acme and riyadh-grill and applies migrations. Verdict: fail. Blocking: (1) reservations-context.ts caches 60 s fresh / 5 min stale with no failure cooldown instead of the contract's and architecture's 5 min / 24 h / 30 s (its test asserts the deviation); (2) no code path enforces hasProvisionedDb, so an active but unprovisioned organization is served a freshly created empty tenant DB instead of a uniform refusal, unlike the staffing mirror staff-auth.ts:167; (3) reservations-security.test.ts omits the tenant-api-operator audience, over-long-TTL and impersonated-write token cases that VAL-FND-020 and library/staffing-patterns.md:94 require across every mounted route; (4) _layout.tsx never hides the location picker for a single-location organization (VAL-FND-022), visible on riyadh-grill; (5) docs/permissions.md, docs/reservations-contract.md and ADR 048 list permission, claim, audience and header names that do not exist in the code, so the 8 implemented permissions and 6 flags are not the ones documented (VAL-FND-024). Non-blocking: 7 role presets vs the contract's 4 (the required four have exact grant sets), the trigger-error string mismatch in mapSqliteConstraintError ('overlap_conflict' vs 'table_overlap'), ADR draft topic gaps, the replay path skipping a day-version bump, the settings scaffold bypassing withReservationWrite, the public scaffolds' fail-open flag check, and the unused notifyReservationsContextChanged helper.
